title: Cross-border GPU Onboard Checklist and Forecast — Q4 2026
summary: Working operational sheet for coordinating multi-cloud GPU onboarding across North America, Europe, and APAC for late-2026. Primary goal: stage node activations in three 3-week sprints per region to smooth utilization, preserve headroom for burst windows, and align with Dedicated customer commitments. This doc combines an activation checklist, week-by-week node targets, expected utilization %, and short remediation playbooks for common failure modes.
assumptions: 1) Target models to serve: mixture of 8-bit quantized decoder LLMs and 16-bit encoder-decoder for rerank workloads; 2) Default node = 8xA100-equivalent slot; 3) Typical baseline utilization target after warmup: 55–70% during standard hours; 4) Burst allowance: add buffer nodes equal to 15% of active fleet per region for first 6 weeks; 5) Cross-region failover latency budget: 200ms extra tail p99 acceptable for emergency routing.

rollout_timeline:
2026-09-06 to 2026-09-26 (NA Sprint 1 & 2): provision 240 -> 400 active slots across two clouds; validate autoscale hooks; run cost telemetry.
2026-09-13 to 2026-10-03 (EU Sprint 1 & 2): stagger activations across zones for resilience tests; run compliance audit for customer data paths.
2026-09-20 to 2026-10-11 (APAC Sprint 1 & 2): use conservative slot counts first, validate spot/interrupt handling for cost efficiency.
Cutover windows: nightly low-traffic windows between 02:00–05:00 local time for each region; coordinate with SRE on retention policies and Kubernetes draining steps.
utilization_smoothing_plan:
- Progressive ramp: move from 20% to target utilization over 10 business days with automated promotable routes.
- Prefix cache warmers pre-seed 5% of high-frequency keys before customer rollouts.
- Batching config: start with conservative max_batch=8, increase to 32 after 72h stable telemetry.
- Dynamic routing: route low-latency customers to dedicated pools, route bulk/async to lower-cost variants to preserve p99 SLOs.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: sudden supply shortage in a cloud zone -> Mitigation: cross-cloud fallback plan + pre-reserved buffer in adjacent zone.
Risk: higher-than-expected QPS from PLG -> Mitigation: throttling policy + burst queues + on-demand scale-up runbook.
Risk: kernel incompatibility with new quantized model -> Mitigation: holdback nodes for canary builds and run nightly perf regressions.
